content: A motor vehicle accident, also referred to as a traffic collision, occurs when a vehicle comes into contact with another vehicle, a pedestrian, an animal, road debris, or a stationary object such as a tree or a utility pole. These incidents can result in a range of outcomes, including physical injuries, fatalities, damage to the vehicles involved, and destruction of property. Several factors contribute to the likelihood of a traffic collision. These include the design and structural integrity of the vehicle, the speed at which the vehicle is being operated, the design and condition of the road, the surrounding road environment, the skill level of the driver, any impairments affecting the driver, and the driver’s behavior while operating the vehicle. Globally, motor vehicle collisions are a significant cause of death and disability. They also impose substantial financial burdens on both society as a whole and the individuals directly involved in these incidents. Traffic collisions can be categorized based on their general type. Common classifications include head-on collisions, road departure accidents, rear-end collisions, side-impact collisions, and rollover accidents.
